title: Unified plugin registry & lifecycle for load/perf harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: The existing load/perf harness uses a collection of ad-hoc loader adapters, runner hooks, and sidecar shims. Over time this has created fragile integration points, duplicated lifecycle logic (init/teardown), and made it hard to add new plugins (e.g., KV-cache simulators, custom telemetry, request-transformers) without touching core code. Goal: Introduce a small, well-documented plugin registry and lifecycle API that unifies discovery, configuration, and safe hot-reload of harness extensions. The API should support synchronous and asynchronous plugins, dependency ordering, and clear error isolation so a failing plugin does not crash a run. This refactor is intended to reduce future onboarding time for new plugin types, eliminate several brittle test-only shims, and enable safer remote configuration of instrumentation plugins for regression runs.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Plugins are discovered via a single registry (code + entrypoint) and loaded through a documented factory interface
A2: Plugins expose start()/stop()/on_event() lifecycle hooks; harness calls are deterministic for setup and teardown
A3: Existing adapters (http-load-adapter, grpc-simulator, prefix-cache) are ported to the registry with tests and show no behavior regressions
A4: Failures inside a plugin result in an isolated error logged to the harness UI and do not abort the entire run by default
A5: New plugin can be added via configuration alone (no code changes to core harness) in the CI smoke job
A6: Performance regression baseline shows <=1% variance attributable to the refactor on 95th percentile latency across our synthetic corpora
changes: Introduce plugin_registry module with register()/get()/reload() primitives
Define PluginBase abstract interface (start, stop, on_event, metadata) and async compatibility shim
Port three existing adapters (http, grpc, kvprefix) to the new API and add integration tests
Add config-driven plugin activation with environment-scoped overrides for CI and local runs
Add health/isolation wrapper that traps plugin exceptions and surfaces them to harness metrics and logs
Update CI smoke/regression job to run a matrix with and without the plugin registry to validate parity
testing_plan: Unit tests for plugin_registry: registration, lookup, reload semantics, and ordering
Integration tests: run full synthetic load scenario with ported adapters and compare traces/latency to golden run
Chaos test: inject plugin failures and timeouts to validate isolation and harness resilience
CI perf check: run perf-regression-suite (small corpus) before/after and assert <1% deviation
Manual review: run a dedicated smoke run against preprod Dedicated cluster to validate deployment interactions
rollout_plan: Feature branch -> PR with experimental flag 'use_plugin_registry' off by default
Merge gated by unit and integration tests + perf smoke comparisons
Enable flag in CI smoke/regression jobs and run 3 consecutive daily runs to collect variance
Gradually enable flag in canary harness runs (non-customer traffic) for 48h
Flip default flag in next minor release once metrics and traces validate stability
Post-rollout: deprecate old adapter entrypoints and remove after one release cycle
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: subtle behavioral differences between old adapters and ported plugins could affect perf. Mitigation: keep old code paths behind feature flag and run A/B comparisons in CI.
Risk: slow plugin initialization adds latency to harness start. Mitigation: add timeout and concurrent init with ordered readiness checks; document expected init time in plugin metadata.
Risk: plugin exceptions could corrupt test state. Mitigation: health wrapper isolates exceptions and records trace-level diagnostics, plugin runs are sandboxed where possible.
Risk: config explosion across CI and local environments. Mitigation: provide sane defaults and a single central config schema + validator
